verdict.reason: Both debates converge on pause, log, and reintroduce one at a time with a severity ceiling, but B's objections do more work: the patch-test trap leads to a pair-testing stage, and the caution-versus-nocebo pushback produces a narrower, observable severity rule. A has a well-earned standing disagreement about test order, but spends a turn speculating about the user's motive, which nothing downstream uses. B's conditional map also adds an interaction branch that A never reaches.

comparisons.a_observation: The Bias Spotter speculates about why the user is asking (money, attachment, a trusted recommendation); the Experimenter dismisses it in the next turn and it changes nothing in the plan.
comparisons.b_observation: The Bias Watcher objects that a forearm patch is not facial skin and that reactions can be delayed or appear only when products are layered; Mill answers by adding a pair-testing stage (B.debate[6].text), so the method changes because of the objection.
comparisons.why_it_matters: With three products started together, an interaction between them is a real possibility. B's plan can detect it, while A's one-at-a-time protocol could clear every product and leave the user without an answer.

comparisons.a_observation: The Experimenter partly concedes on blind ordering but keeps that the prime suspect should go first, which leaves a clear, useful disagreement about order.
comparisons.b_observation: After the Bias Watcher pushes back that some tingling is expected (B.debate[8].text), the Subtractor narrows his removal rule to stinging that persists or comes with redness, tightness or peeling, and names the cause of the change.
comparisons.why_it_matters: Whether the sting is a normal tingle or a reason to stop is the user's first fork. B's narrowed rule gives signs the user can observe, while A's order dispute is useful but matters less.

comparisons.a_observation: Covers the mild versus red-flag branches and the case where the sting persists on bare skin. It includes trouble breathing.
comparisons.b_observation: Covers the same branches and adds a combination-only branch with pair testing, non-skincare causes including shaving and existing skin conditions, and a clinician who can run patch testing.
comparisons.why_it_matters: B's extra branch is the one most specific to starting three products at once, so it gives the user one more condition they can check.

verdict.best_of_a: A.debate[10].text: The suggestion to start with the least-suspected product, or let someone else pick the order, is a concrete guard against confirmation bias. It produces a standing disagreement that is clearly stated.
verdict.best_of_b: B.debate[6].text: The pair-testing stage for interacting products, such as acids with a retinoid, is explicitly marked as the mind's own extension rather than something Mill wrote.

concerns.description: The point that expecting harm can amplify a sensation is closer to the nocebo literature than to Thinking, Fast and Slow. It is not flagged as the mind's own extension.
Speculates about the user's motive for asking, which the input does not support. The next turn sets it aside.
